scenes.narration: Tell Claude the staging server is called acorn. Clear the session, and ask again. Without a memory, it's gone. Claude forgets. Cogi doesn't.
Cogi is a free, long-term memory for Claude Code. It keeps every message you and Claude exchange, word for word, with the time it was said.
It all stays in one folder on your own computer. No account, no API key, and no AI calls to save a message.
When something has dropped out of the conversation, Claude searches Cogi and gets your exact words back. Here, it answers: acorn.
I tested it on a public benchmark with over a million tokens of history. It found the right past session in its top five, ninety-three percent of the time.
It's open source and installs with one command. My tip: when it matters, ask Claude to check its memory. Try it, and tell me what it brings back.
